```{python}
#| label: setup
import json, pathlib
import pandas as pd
R = json.loads(pathlib.Path("analysis/results.json").read_text())
ROLE = json.loads(pathlib.Path("analysis/role_names.json").read_text())
ROLE4 = json.loads(pathlib.Path("analysis/role_names_K4.json").read_text())
A, RF = R["paper_a"], R["roles_final"]
F5, F4 = RF["nihai"]["K5"], RF["nihai"]["K4"]
SC = RF["tarama"]
COV = RF["kovaryans"]
M5, M4 = R["lineup_model_roles_final_K5"], R["lineup_model_roles_final_K4"]
D5 = M5["ayristirma"]
F0T, F2T = R["formula_test_corrected_min0_tezarketip"], R["formula_test_corrected_min2_tezarketip"]
n = lambda x: f"{x:,}"
pct = lambda x, d=0: f"{100 * x:.{d}f}%"
f2 = lambda x: f"{x:.2f}"
def fp(p):
    return "< .001" if p < 0.001 else f"= {p:.3f}".replace("0.", ".")
def share(k, role, pos):
    t = F5["pozisyon"][str(role)]
    return t.get(pos, 0) / sum(t.values())
J5 = F5["jaccard_kume"]
stable_roles = sum(j >= 0.75 for j in J5)
weakest = min(range(len(J5)), key=lambda i: J5[i]) + 1
P = M5["guc"]
pair = " × ".join(ROLE[str(i)].lower() for i in P["cift"])
def _term(t):
    a = t.replace("n", "").split("×")
    return " + ".join(ROLE[x].lower() for x in a) if len(a) == 2 else ROLE[a[0]].lower() + " count"
_pos = [(t, v) for t, v in M5["rol_bilesimi"]["en_buyuk_katsayilar"].items() if v > 0 and "×" in t][:3]
TOP = "; ".join(f"{_term(t)} ({v:+.2f})" for t, v in _pos)
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"**Purpose:** Data-driven player roles are increasingly used to describe positionless basketball and to guide lineup construction, but the stability of such roles and their value for explaining lineup performance beyond player quality are rarely tested. "
f"**Methods:** All EuroLeague games from 2016–17 to 2024–25 ({n(A['games'])} games) were analysed using official box scores, play-by-play, shot coordinates and assist links. "
f"Role variables (possession shares with on-court denominators, shot profile and assist-network indicators) were clustered with Gaussian mixture models in {n(RF['fit_N'])} player-seasons; the number of roles was chosen by player-level bootstrap stability. "
f"Role composition was then tested against lineup net rating, with regularised adjusted plus-minus (RAPM) controlling for player quality, in an out-of-time validation with a role-label permutation test. "
f"**Results:** Five roles were retained (mean bootstrap Jaccard {f2(F5['jaccard_ort'])}; {stable_roles} of 5 roles ≥ 0.75), whereas six or more roles were unstable, as was a previously used seven-cluster solution (mean Jaccard {f2(A['thesis_ward7_jaccard_mean'])}). "
f"Ball handlers and rim protectors were almost exclusively guards and centres, respectively, whereas wing, stretch-forward and interior-big roles drew on two positions (Cramér's V = {f2(F5['cramers_v'])}). "
f"Adding role composition to RAPM improved out-of-time prediction more than permuted role labels did (p {fp(M5['rol_bilesimi']['p'])}), but the gain came from the number of players in each role (p {fp(D5['sayilar_p'])}), not from role pairings, and its effects were about a quarter as large as differences in player quality. "
f"**Conclusions:** Five functional roles can be recovered reproducibly from open EuroLeague data. Role labels carry a small amount of information about lineup performance beyond regularised player ratings, but there was no evidence of synergy between roles.")
```

# Data and code availability {.unnumbered}

All data were obtained from the publicly accessible EuroLeague application programming interface. The code that downloads the data and reproduces every number, table and figure is available at https://github.com/koksalahmet85-svg/sports-science-paper-engine and will be archived with a persistent identifier on acceptance.

A generative AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) was used to assist with literature search, programming and language editing.
